chunks: And from him, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Shuʿayb ibn Yaʿqūb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in the houses of the Magians. He said: “Sprinkle and pray.”
Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Salat (prayer) is not valid in a garment that wine, an intoxicating drink, or fuqqāʿ has touched, until it is purified by washing.
Its explanation has already passed in full in the Book of Ṭahārah, with nothing further to add, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.
Then he, may Allah have mercy on him, said: One does not pray in a garment containing semen until it is washed; and likewise is the ruling concerning the rest of the impurities.
What pertains to that has also already passed in the Book of Ṭahārah, and that which confirms it is what he narrated:

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual worship under discussion
key_terms.النَّجَاسَاتِ: ritual impurities, the broader category to which the same ruling applies
key_terms.الْغَسْلِ: washing, the means of purification required here
key_terms.بُيُوتِ الْمَجُوسِ: the houses of the Magians, referring to a place in which prayer is being considered
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: wine, a ritually impure intoxicant mentioned as contaminating clothing
key_terms.رُشَّ: sprinkle, meaning to apply water before praying
key_terms.فُقَّاعٌ: fuqqāʿ, an intoxicating beverage mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.مَنِيٌّ: semen, cited as a substance requiring washing before prayer in the garment

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in a place or garment affected by najasah or intoxicants?
ai.summary: This passage gives legal rulings on the validity of salat (prayer) with respect to place and clothing. It permits praying in the houses of the Magians after sprinkling, and it states that prayer is not valid in garments contaminated by intoxicants, semen, or other najasah until they are washed and purified.
